profile.headline: Software Engineer, DACA Recipient.
profile.summary:
In 2017 I've had the opportunity to work in Artificial Intelligence my role as an engineer was to work with various talented Engineers from Universities like Stanford and CMU. I also learned about embedded devices and a little bit about cars and how Teslas were put together. I almost burned one while trying to show case it at CES 2017 Las Vegas. I also worked as a contractor doing IT/Devops work for friends and other startups.

I am currently a Full Stack Software Engineer at the Superior Court of California.

positions.title: Renewable Energy Intern
positions.description: As a result of increased use of renewable energy sources for power generation, the overall quality of electrical services has degraded due to its instability caused by reliance on natural factors. We developed a method that uses power frequency as an indication of the quality of power supplied by the grid, and regulates it by rescheduling load consumption. We thus designed and implemented an embedded system in a micro-grid testbed that regulates power frequency through control of the deferrable loads in order to demonstrate its feasibility and efficacy in solving a severe problem that affects the actual power grid. Frequency measurements from a microcontroller’s counting hardware feature are transmitted wirelessly, using XBee radios, to a single board computer for further processing. The computer then runs an algorithm that processes this information and determines when to turn on/off or change the threshold temperature of the various deferrable loads while accounting for certain aspects unique to each load, all with minimal impact on the consumers. Considering these aspects, such as duty cycle, allows the micro-grid testbed to stabilize frequency without drastically changing the behavior of the loads. This regulation of the quality of power from the power grid prevents crises such as blackouts in a variety of situations – both emergency situations and everyday deviations – with imperceptible effect on the consumers.
